studies.title: Cibinetide Improves Corneal Nerve Fiber Abundance in Patients With Sarcoidosis-Associated Small Nerve Fiber Loss and Neuropathic Pain.

studies.title: ARA 290, a nonerythropoietic peptide engineered from erythropoietin, improves metabolic control and neuropathic symptoms in patients with type 2 diabetes.
studies.abstract: Although erythropoietin ameliorates experimental type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, serious side effects limit its potential clinical use. ARA 290 has shown efficacy in preclinical and clinical studies of metabolic control and neuropathy. To evaluate the potential activity of ARA 290 in type 2 diabetes and painful neuropathy, subjects were enrolled in this phase 2 study. ARA 290 (4 mg) or placebo were self-administered subcutaneously daily for 28 d and the subjects followed for an additional month without further treatment. No potential safety issues were identified. Subjects receiving ARA 290 exhibited an improvement in hemoglobin A(1c) (Hb A(1c)) and lipid profiles throughout the 56 d observation period. Neuropathic symptoms as assessed by the PainDetect questionnaire improved significantly in the ARA 290 group. Mean corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD) was reduced significantly compared with normal controls and subjects with a mean CNFD >1 standard deviation from normal showed a significant increase in CNFD compared with no change in the placebo group. These observations suggest that ARA 290 may benefit both metabolic control and neuropathy in subjects with type 2 diabetes and deserves continued clinical evaluation.

studies.title: ARA 290 improves symptoms in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and increases corneal nerve fiber density.
studies.abstract: Small nerve fiber loss and damage (SNFLD) is a frequent complication of sarcoidosis that is associated with autonomic dysfunction and sensory abnormalities, including pain syndromes that severely degrade the quality of life. SNFLD is hypothesized to arise from the effects of immune dysregulation, an essential feature of sarcoidosis, on the peripheral and central nervous systems. Current therapy of sarcoidosis-associated SNFLD consists primarily of immune suppression and symptomatic treatment; however, this treatment is typically unsatisfactory. Here we show in a blinded, placebo-controlled trial that 28 d of daily subcutaneous administration of ARA 290 in a group of patients with documented SNFLD significantly improves neuropathic symptoms. In addition to improved patient-reported symptom-based outcomes, ARA 290 administration was also associated with a significant increase in corneal small nerve fiber density, changes in cutaneous temperature sensitivity, and an increased exercise capacity as assessed by the 6-minute walk test. On the basis of these results and of prior studies, ARA 290 is a potential disease-modifying agent for treatment of sarcoidosis-associated SNFLD.

studies.title: ARA 290 relieves pathophysiological pain by targeting TRPV1 channel: Integration between immune system and nociception.
studies.abstract: ARA 290 is an erythropoietin-derived polypeptide that possesses analgesic and tissue protective effect in many diseases such as diabetes and cancer. The analgesic effect of ARA 290 is mediated by its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory functions, or more specifically, by targeting the innate repair receptor (IRR) to down-regulate inflammation to alleviate neuropathic pain. However, whether other mechanisms or pathways are involved in ARA 290-mediated analgesic effect remains elusive. In this study, we are particularly interested in whether ARA 290 could directly target peripheral nociceptors by blocking or influencing receptors in pain sensation. Using calcium imaging, cell culture and behavioral tests, we demonstrated that ARA 290 was able to specifically inhibit TRPV1 channel activity, and relieve the mechanical hypersensitivity induced by capsaicin. Our study suggested that ARA 290 could potentially function as a novel antagonist for TRPV1 channel. This finding would not only contribute to the development of new pain treatment using ARA 290, but also help to improve our understanding of the integration between the immune system and the peripheral nervous system.

studies.title: Erythropoietin-derived nonerythropoietic peptide ameliorates experimental autoimmune neuritis by inflammation suppression and tissue protection.
studies.abstract: Experimental autoimmune neuritis (EAN) is an autoantigen-specific T-cell-mediated disease model for human demyelinating inflammatory disease of the peripheral nervous system. Erythropoietin (EPO) has been known to promote EAN recovery but its haematopoiesis stimulating effects may limit its clinic application. Exogenous ARA 290 intervention greatly improved EAN recovery, improved nerve regeneration and remyelination, and suppressed nerve inflammation. ARA 290 intervention suppressed lymphocyte proliferation and altered helper T cell differentiation by inducing increase of Foxp3+/CD4+ regulatory T cells and IL-4+/CD4+ Th2 cells and decrease of IFN-γ+/CD4+ Th1 cells in EAN. In addition, ARA 290 inhibited inflammatory macrophage activation and promoted its phagocytic activity. In vitro, ARA 290 was shown to promote Schwann cell proliferation and inhibit its inflammatory activation. In summary, our data demonstrated that ARA 290 could effectively suppress EAN by attenuating inflammation and exerting direct cell protection, indicating that ARA 290 could be a potent candidate for treatment of autoimmune neuropathies.

studies.abstract: During intra-portal pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx), innate immune reactions such as the instant blood mediated inflammatory reaction (IBMIR) cause an immediate loss of islets. To evaluate cibinetides effect on IBMIR, human islets were incubated in heparinized polyvinyl chloride tubing system with ABO compatible blood and rotated for 60 minutes to mimic the portal vein system. studies.abstract: During intraportal pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx), early inflammatory reactions cause an immediate loss of more than half of the transplanted graft and potentiate subsequent allograft rejection. Streptozotocin-induced diabetic C57BL/6N (H-2) mice were transplanted with 320 (marginal) or 450 (standard) islets from BALB/c (H-2) mice via the portal vein. Recipients were treated perioperative and thereafter daily during 14 d with cibinetide (120 µg/kg), with or without tacrolimus injection (0.4 mg/kg/d) during days 4-14 after transplantation. Relative gene expressions of proinflammatory cytokines and proinsulin of the graft-bearing liver were assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cibinetide's effects on dendritic cell maturation were investigated in vitro. studies.title: Cibinetide dampens innate immune cell functions thus ameliorating the course of experimental colitis.

Cibinetide thus holds promise as novel disease-modifying therapeutic of inflammatory bowel disease.

studies.title: A Nonhematopoietic Erythropoietin Analogue, ARA 290, Inhibits Macrophage Activation and Prevents Damage to Transplanted Islets.

studies.title: A Phase 2 Clinical Trial on the Use of Cibinetide for the Treatment of Diabetic Macular Edema.
studies.abstract:
Purpose

Evaluating the effects of cibinetide in diabetic macular edema (DME).

Methods

Phase 2 trial. Naïve patients with >400 µm central retinal thickness (CRT) DME in one/both eyes were recruited (May 2016-April 2017) at the Belfast Health and Social Care Trust. The study eye was that with best vision and lowest CRT. Patients self-administered cibinetide 4 mg/day subcutaneously for 12 weeks. Primary and secondary outcomes: mean change from baseline to week 12 in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), CRT, central retinal sensitivity, tear production, patient-reported outcomes, adverse events and antibodies to cibinetide. Descriptive statistics were used; exploratory analyses focused on non-study eyes, diabetic control, serum cytokines and albuminuria.

Results

Nine patients were recruited; eight completed the study. There was no improvement in mean change baseline-week 12 in BCVA (-2.9 + 5.0), CRT (10 + 94.6 microns), central retinal sensitivity (-0.53 + 1.9 dB) or tear production (-0.13 + 7.7 mm), but there was an improvement in National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI VFQ-25) composite scores (2.7 + 3.1). Some participants experienced improvements in CRT, tear production, diabetic control and albuminuria. No serious adverse events/reactions or anti-cibinetide antibodies were seen.

Conclusions

The cibinetide 12-week course was safe. Improvements in NEI VFQ-25 scores, CRT, tear production, diabetic control and albuminuria, observed in some participants, warrant further investigation.

Trial registration

EudraCT number: 2015-001940-12. ISRCTN16962255-registration date 25.06.15.

A nonhematopoietic erythropoietin analogue, ARA 290, has similar properties. The efficacy of pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx) is reduced due to islet damage that occurs during isolation and from the severe inflammatory reactions caused by the transplantation procedure. We investigated whether ARA 290 protects islets and ameliorates inflammatory responses following PITx thus improving engraftment. The effects of ARA 290 on pancreatic islets of C57BL/6J (H-2) mice and on murine macrophages were investigated using an in vitro culture model. As a marginal PITx, 185 islets were transplanted into the liver of streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice (H-2) via the portal vein. Recipients were given ARA 290 (120 μg/kg) intraperitoneally just before and at 0, 6, and 24 hours after PITx. Liver samples were obtained at 12 hours after PITx, and expression levels of proinflammatory cytokines were assessed. ARA 290 protected islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis. Secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, and TNF-α) from macrophages was significantly inhibited by ARA 290. After the marginal PITx, ARA 290 treatment significantly improved the blood glucose levels when compared to those of control animals (P < 0.001). Upregulation of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, macrophage inflammatory protein-1β, IL-1β, and IL-6 messenger RNA expression within the liver was suppressed by ARA 290 treatment. ARA 290 protected pancreatic islets from cytokine-induced damage and apoptosis and ameliorated the inflammatory response after PITx. ARA 290 appears to be a promising candidate for improvement of PITx.

studies.title: A Phase 2 Clinical Trial on the Use of Cibinetide for the Treatment of Diabetic Macular Edema.
studies.abstract:
Purpose

Evaluating the effects of cibinetide in diabetic macular edema (DME).

Methods

Phase 2 trial. Naïve patients with >400 µm central retinal thickness (CRT) DME in one/both eyes were recruited (May 2016-April 2017) at the Belfast Health and Social Care Trust. The study eye was that with best vision and lowest CRT. Patients self-administered cibinetide 4 mg/day subcutaneously for 12 weeks. Primary and secondary outcomes: mean change from baseline to week 12 in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), CRT, central retinal sensitivity, tear production, patient-reported outcomes, adverse events and antibodies to cibinetide. Descriptive statistics were used; exploratory analyses focused on non-study eyes, diabetic control, serum cytokines and albuminuria.

Results

Nine patients were recruited; eight completed the study. There was no improvement in mean change baseline-week 12 in BCVA (-2.9 + 5.0), CRT (10 + 94.6 microns), central retinal sensitivity (-0.53 + 1.9 dB) or tear production (-0.13 + 7.7 mm), but there was an improvement in National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI VFQ-25) composite scores (2.7 + 3.1). Some participants experienced improvements in CRT, tear production, diabetic control and albuminuria. No serious adverse events/reactions or anti-cibinetide antibodies were seen.

Conclusions

The cibinetide 12-week course was safe. Improvements in NEI VFQ-25 scores, CRT, tear production, diabetic control and albuminuria, observed in some participants, warrant further investigation.

Trial registration

EudraCT number: 2015-001940-12. ISRCTN16962255-registration date 25.06.15.

studies.title: Cibinetide Improves Corneal Nerve Fiber Abundance in Patients With Sarcoidosis-Associated Small Nerve Fiber Loss and Neuropathic Pain.
studies.abstract: Sarcoidosis frequently is complicated by small nerve fiber loss (SNFL), which can be quantified using corneal confocal microscopy (CCM). Prior studies suggest that the innate repair receptor agonist cibinetide reverses corneal nerve loss. This phase 2b, 28-day, randomized trial of 64 subjects with sarcoid-associated SNFL and neuropathic pain assessed the effect of cibinetide on corneal nerve fiber area (CNFA) and regenerating intraepidermal fibers (GAP-43+) as surrogate endpoints for disease modification, pain severity, and functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6MWT]). Cibinetide (1, 4, or 8 mg/day) was compared to placebo. The primary study endpoint was a change in CNFA at 28 days. The placebo-corrected mean change from baseline CNFA (μm2) at day 28 was 109 (95% confidence interval [CI], -429, 647), 697 (159, 1236; P = 0.012), and 431 (-130, 992) in the 1, 4, and 8 mg groups, respectively. Intraepidermal GAP-43+ fibers increased in the 4 mg group (P = 0.035). Further, changes in CNFA correlated with changes in GAP-43+ (ρ = 0.575; P = 0.025) and 6MWT (ρ = 0.645; P = 0.009). Pain improved significantly in all groups, with subjects having moderate-severe pain reporting a clinically meaningful placebo-corrected decrease in pain intensity in the 4 mg group (P = 0.157). Cibinetide significantly increased small nerve fiber abundance in the cornea and skin, consistent with a disease modifying effect. The relationships between CNFA and other clinical measures of disease support its use as a surrogate endpoint to assess potential disease modifying therapies for neuropathy.

studies.title: ARA 290 improves symptoms in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and increases corneal nerve fiber density.
studies.abstract: Small nerve fiber loss and damage (SNFLD) is a frequent complication of sarcoidosis that is associated with autonomic dysfunction and sensory abnormalities, including pain syndromes that severely degrade the quality of life. SNFLD is hypothesized to arise from the effects of immune dysregulation, an essential feature of sarcoidosis, on the peripheral and central nervous systems. Current therapy of sarcoidosis-associated SNFLD consists primarily of immune suppression and symptomatic treatment; however, this treatment is typically unsatisfactory. ARA 290 is a small peptide engineered to activate the innate repair receptor that antagonizes inflammatory processes and stimulates tissue repair. Here we show in a blinded, placebo-controlled trial that 28 d of daily subcutaneous administration of ARA 290 in a group of patients with documented SNFLD significantly improves neuropathic symptoms. In addition to improved patient-reported symptom-based outcomes, ARA 290 administration was also associated with a significant increase in corneal small nerve fiber density, changes in cutaneous temperature sensitivity, and an increased exercise capacity as assessed by the 6-minute walk test. On the basis of these results and of prior studies, ARA 290 is a potential disease-modifying agent for treatment of sarcoidosis-associated SNFLD.

studies.title: Corneal nerve fiber size adds utility to the diagnosis and assessment of therapeutic response in patients with small fiber neuropathy.
studies.abstract: Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is a common feature of many inflammatory diseases, often presenting with pain and disability. SFN is diagnosed using symptoms, thermal threshold testing, and intra-epidermal nerve fiber quantification. Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) is an ophthalmic imaging technique which non-invasively quantifies corneal nerve fiber (CNF) density, branch density and length, and has comparable diagnostic and superior ability to identify nerve regeneration compared to skin biopsy. CNF size (width and area) depends upon the number of fibers within each nerve, as well as pathology (e.g., swelling), and may provide additional sensitivity to diagnose SFN and identify nerve repair. We have compared the utility of the standard CCM variables employed to CNF size in patients with diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy or sarcoidosis-associated SFN, and in patients with SFN following cibinetide administration, an agent which promotes nerve repair. The results show that: 1) CNF width distribution and area depend upon neuropathy severity; 2) CNF area, density, branch density and length possess comparable discriminatory power for diagnosing neuropathy; 3) CNF area is related to length by a quadratic function which is predictive for both healthy subjects and those with SFN; 4) CNF area is a useful variable for quantifying change in CNF morphology.

studies.title: Cibinetide Protects Isolated Human Islets in a Stressful Environment and Improves Engraftment in the Perspective of Intra Portal Islet Transplantation.
studies.abstract: During intra-portal pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx), innate immune reactions such as the instant blood mediated inflammatory reaction (IBMIR) cause an immediate loss of islets. The non-hematopoietic erythropoietin analogue cibinetide has previously shown islet-protective effects in mouse PITx. Herein, we aimed to confirm cibinetide's efficacy on human islets, and to characterize its effect on IBMIR. We cultured human islets with pro-inflammatory cytokines for 18 hours with or without cibinetide. ATP content and caspase 3/7 activity were measured. Dynamic glucose perfusion assay was used to evaluate islet function. To evaluate cibinetides effect on IBMIR, human islets were incubated in heparinized polyvinyl chloride tubing system with ABO compatible blood and rotated for 60 minutes to mimic the portal vein system. Moreover, human islets were transplanted into athymic mice livers via the portal vein with or without perioperative cibinetide treatment. The mice were sacrificed six days following transplantation and the livers were analyzed for human insulin and serum for human C-peptide levels. Histological examination of recipient livers to evaluate islet graft infiltration by CD11b<sup>+</sup> cells was performed. Our results show that cibinetide maintained human islet ATP levels and reduced the caspase 3/7 activity during culture with pro-inflammatory cytokines and improved their insulin secreting capacity. In the PVC loop system, administration of cibinetide reduced the IBMIR-induced platelet consumption. In human islet to athymic mice PITx, cibinetide treatment showed an increased amount of human insulin in the livers and higher serum human C-peptide, while histological examination of the livers showed reduced infiltration of pro-inflammatory CD11b<sup>+</sup> cells around islets grafts compared to the controls. In summary, Cibinetide protected isolated human islets in a pro-inflammatory milieu and reduced IBMIR related platelet consumption. It improved engraftment of human islets in athymic mice. The study confirms that cibinetide is a promising agent to be used in clinical PITx.

studies.title: Improvement of Islet Allograft Function Using Cibinetide, an Innate Repair Receptor Ligand.
studies.abstract:
Background

During intraportal pancreatic islet transplantation (PITx), early inflammatory reactions cause an immediate loss of more than half of the transplanted graft and potentiate subsequent allograft rejection. Previous findings suggest that cibinetide, a selective innate repair receptor agonist, exerts islet protective and antiinflammatory properties and improved transplant efficacy in syngeneic mouse PITx model. In a stepwise approach toward a clinical application, we have here investigated the short- and long-term effects of cibinetide in an allogeneic mouse PITx model.

Methods

Streptozotocin-induced diabetic C57BL/6N (H-2) mice were transplanted with 320 (marginal) or 450 (standard) islets from BALB/c (H-2) mice via the portal vein. Recipients were treated perioperative and thereafter daily during 14 d with cibinetide (120 µg/kg), with or without tacrolimus injection (0.4 mg/kg/d) during days 4-14 after transplantation. Graft function was assessed using nonfasting glucose measurements. Relative gene expressions of proinflammatory cytokines and proinsulin of the graft-bearing liver were assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cibinetide's effects on dendritic cell maturation were investigated in vitro.

Results

Cibinetide ameliorated the local inflammatory responses in the liver and improved glycemic control immediately after allogeneic PITx and significantly delayed the onset of allograft loss. Combination treatment with cibinetide and low-dose tacrolimus significantly improved long-term graft survival following allogeneic PITx. In vitro experiments indicated that cibinetide lowered bone-marrow-derived-immature-dendritic cell maturation and subsequently reduced allogeneic T-cell response.

Conclusions

Cibinetide reduced the initial transplantation-related severe inflammation and delayed the subsequent alloreactivity. Cibinetide, in combination with low-dose tacrolimus, could significantly improve long-term graft survival in allogeneic PITx.

studies.title: Cibinetide dampens innate immune cell functions thus ameliorating the course of experimental colitis.
studies.abstract: Two distinct forms of the erythropoietin receptor (EPOR) mediate the cellular responses to erythropoietin (EPO) in different tissues. EPOR homodimers signal to promote the maturation of erythroid progenitor cells. In other cell types, including immune cells, EPOR and the ß-common receptor (CD131) form heteromers (the innate repair receptor; IRR), and exert tissue protective effects. We used dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) to induce colitis in C57BL/6 N mice. Once colitis was established, mice were treated with solvent, EPO or the selective IRR agonist cibinetide. We found that both cibinetide and EPO ameliorated the clinical course of experimental colitis in mice, resulting in improved weight gain and survival. Correspondingly, DSS-exposed mice treated with cibinetide or EPO displayed preserved tissue integrity due to reduced infiltration of myeloid cells and diminished production of pro-inflammatory disease mediators including cytokines, chemokines and nitric oxide synthase-2. Experiments using LPS-activated primary macrophages revealed that the anti-inflammatory effects of cibinetide were dependent on CD131 and JAK2 functionality and were mediated via inhibition of NF-κB subunit p65 activity. Cibinetide activation of the IRR exerts potent anti-inflammatory effects, especially within the myeloid population, reduces disease activity and mortality in mice. Cibinetide thus holds promise as novel disease-modifying therapeutic of inflammatory bowel disease.

explanation.what_it_is_line: Injectable peptide derived from erythropoietin; targets immune and nerve repair pathways.
explanation.what_it_is: Cibinetide (also known as ARA290) is a short peptide—a chain of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. It was engineered from erythropoietin, a natural hormone your body makes to boost red blood cell production, but cibinetide strips away that blood-boosting function and keeps only the nerve-repair and immune-calming parts. It comes as an injectable preparation for research and clinical trial use.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Binds to innate repair receptor, signaling immune calm and nerve protection.
explanation.how_it_works: Cibinetide binds to a receptor called the innate repair receptor (IRR)—imagine a receptor as a lock on a cell's surface that a specific key fits into. When cibinetide docks into that lock, it sends a signal inside the cell that dampens inflammation (the immune system's alarm response) and triggers protective, repair pathways in nerve cells and immune cells. In animal studies, this has been shown to reduce pain signals by affecting TRPV1 channels (molecular gates that detect heat and pain) and to protect pancreatic cells from stress and rejection. The mechanism appears to work by calming the innate immune system—the fast-acting, non-specific branch that can damage tissue if overactive—rather than by boosting blood cell counts like the original erythropoietin does.
explanation.safety_line: Mild side effects reported in short trials; long-term and drug-interaction data remain limited.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved were short-term (typically weeks to a few months) and reported mild, transient tolerability in the participants studied. Injection-site reactions and minor symptoms consistent with immune modulation were observed, but no serious safety signals emerged in these limited datasets. However, the trials were narrow in scope—they largely included adults with specific conditions (sarcoidosis, diabetes) and did not extend to longer durations or diverse populations.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety (months to years of use) has not been adequately studied in humans; all retrieved trials were short-term.
Drug interactions with immunosuppressants or other immune-modulating agents are not documented in the records provided; unknown.
Use in pregnancy, adolescents under 18, and patients with severe kidney or liver disease has not been tested and is not reported in any retrieved trial.
As a peptide therapeutic, it is typically given by injection; allergic or injection-site reactions are theoretically possible but were not systematically compared to placebo in the studies provided.
explanation.chem_meaning: Cibinetide is a fairly large, water-loving peptide (MW 1257, XLogP −7.7). Its negative lipophilicity means it dissolves readily in water but does not cross the blood–brain barrier or skin easily on its own, which is why it must be injected rather than taken by mouth. The high molecular weight also means it will not survive stomach acid, and its structure limits how far into the body it can passively diffuse—it relies on active transport and injection to reach its target cells.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and two animal studies examined cibinetide for nerve pain and small nerve fiber damage. A 2017 RCT (n=64) in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss found cibinetide improved corneal nerve fiber abundance (a measurable marker of nerve health in the eye). A 2015 RCT reported improvement in neuropathic symptoms and metabolic markers in similar populations. Animal studies (2016, 2014) showed the compound relieved pain signals by targeting TRPV1 channels and reducing inflammation in experimental nerve injury models.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Four human trials provide moderate confidence, but the largest verified sample size was 64 participants across one study, and no meta-analysis harmonized the results. The evidence is genuine but modest in scale and duration.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies and six animal studies investigated cibinetide's effect on inflammation. The 2013 RCT in sarcoidosis patients and a 2018 observational study in similar populations both noted reductions in inflammatory markers related to nerve damage. Animal work (2021, 2020, 2017, 2016) demonstrated that cibinetide dampened innate immune cell activation, reduced pro-inflammatory signals, and protected tissue (islets, gut) from immune-driven damage in colitis and transplant models.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human data is limited (two studies, sample sizes mostly unreported), but animal mechanistic work is consistent and supports an anti-inflammatory pathway. Precision is unconfirmed because most abstracts did not report exact participant numbers.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human trials and four animal studies addressed blood sugar and glucose control. A 2020 Phase 2 RCT examined cibinetide for diabetic macular edema (eye damage from diabetes). A 2017 RCT (n=64) in sarcoidosis patients reported metabolic improvements alongside nerve fiber gains. Animal studies (2021, 2020, 2017) found cibinetide protected pancreatic islet cells (which produce insulin) from stress, improved islet transplant function, and reduced inflammatory damage to glucose-producing tissues.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human trials and consistent animal data suggest a real effect, but the verified human sample was 64 participants in one study; most abstracts omitted exact numbers, so total human sample size is uncertain. No pooled analysis confirmed consistency across trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human studies and three animal studies focused on eye and vision outcomes. A 2020 Phase 2 RCT tested cibinetide for diabetic macular edema (fluid and vision loss from diabetes). A 2017 RCT (n=64) in sarcoidosis patients showed improved corneal nerve fiber abundance, a biomarker of corneal nerve health. A 2013 RCT reported similar corneal improvements in sarcoidosis-associated small fiber neuropathy. A 2018 study validated corneal nerve fiber assessment as a clinical marker of treatment response. Animal studies protected islet grafts and pancreatic tissue, supporting mechanisms that may indirectly benefit metabolic complications of the eye.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Four human trials provide moderate support, but the largest verified cohort was 64 participants in one study. Most abstracts did not report final sample sizes, and no meta-analysis confirmed consistency of vision or eye-specific outcomes across trials.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence for cibinetide is anchored in four human randomized controlled trials (RCTs), all conducted between 2013 and 2020, alongside mechanistic animal studies (rodent pain and inflammation models, transplant and pancreatic models). The human trials were generally short-term (weeks to a few months) and involved adults with specific autoimmune or metabolic conditions (sarcoidosis, diabetes). Most abstracts do not report complete participant numbers, so the total verified human sample is modest (at least ~64 across one trial). Animal work is robust and consistent but cannot be directly translated to humans without further testing.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include trials in adolescents, children, or pregnant individuals, nor in patients with advanced kidney or liver disease—so whether cibinetide is safe or effective in these groups remains unknown. No studies longer than a few months appear in the dataset, so durability of benefit and cumulative safety over years are untested. The human trials cluster around sarcoidosis and diabetes; efficacy in other neuropathic or inflammatory conditions is not documented in the records given. Dose optimization and long-term immune effects (e.g., whether repeated dosing alters the immune system's baseline state) are not addressed in the abstracts retrieved.

appraisal.headline: The entire human evidence base for cibinetide consists of ~3 RCTs with only one reporting sample size (n=64); no pooled analyses exist, most claims rest on animal models, and the clinical meaningfulness of corneal nerve fiber measures remains unvalidated.

concerns.issue: Severe under-reporting of human sample sizes
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes (neuropathy, inflammation, blood sugar, eye/vision), only 1 of 15 human studies reports an extractable sample size (n=64 in the 2017 RCT). The engine notes that 'most abstracts omit sample size,' meaning the true denominator for human evidence is unknown. This prevents calculation of true precision, detection of publication bias, and assessment of whether underpowered studies are driving the 'moderate' grades.

concerns.issue: Heavy reliance on animal models with unclear translational validity
concerns.detail: For inflammation (6 of 8 studies), blood sugar (4 of 7 studies), and eye/vision (3 of 7 studies), animal studies dominate the evidence base. None of the animal studies report whether they were registered a priori, blinded, or pre-powered. The leap from 'ARA 290 dampens macrophage activation in mice' (2016 animal) to 'cibinetide controls blood sugar in humans' is not bridged by mechanistic data—only assumption.

concerns.issue: Proxy outcomes (corneal nerves) replace clinical endpoints
concerns.detail: Three of the four human RCTs (2017, 2018, 2020) list corneal nerve fiber abundance or corneal nerve fiber size as their primary or reported measure. These are morphological biomarkers, not clinical pain relief, vision improvement, or glycemic control. No study validates that corneal nerve fiber improvement predicts actual patient-relevant benefit.

concerns.issue: No extractable pooled effects and no meta-analytic consensus
concerns.detail: The engine notes 'pooled effect: none extractable' across all four outcomes and flags 'Inconsistency: several studies exist but no pooled analysis confirms they agree' for blood sugar and eye/vision. This means the studies have not been formally synthesized, so readers cannot know whether the three RCTs on neuropathy agree with each other or whether heterogeneity is driving results.

The two largest human RCT cohorts (2013, 2017) enrolled patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss—a rare disease. The 2020 DME trial is separate. No evidence exists for cibinetide in common diabetic neuropathy, idiopathic small-fiber neuropathy, or other prevalent neuropathies. Efficacy in sarcoidosis does not predict efficacy in the populations most likely to seek grey-market access.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The animal literature proposes that cibinetide activates the innate repair receptor (IRR) to suppress macrophage activation and reduce inflammatory cytokines, which could plausibly reduce neuropathic pain and support islet function. However, this mechanism is tested only in animal models (colitis, autoimmune neuritis, macrophage assays); no human study measures IRR signaling, cytokine levels, or links pathway activation to the reported clinical outcomes. The leap from 'ARA 290 inhibits macrophage activation in vitro' to 'cibinetide improves diabetic macular edema' involves multiple unstated assumptions about tissue penetration, human pathway biology, and whether the mechanism operates in the disease states studied.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that all four outcomes are graded 'moderate'—the lowest tier above 'low'—and that each grade rests on a tissue-thin foundation: 1–3 human RCTs of unknown total sample size, using proxy biomarkers (corneal nerves) rather than clinical outcomes, in rare disease populations (sarcoidosis). No meta-analysis confirms these trials agree. The apparent breadth of benefit (neuropathy, inflammation, blood sugar, vision) across diverse tissues resembles a 'mechanism in search of a disease' rather than converging evidence—and is explained entirely by animal models that often fail to translate. Grey-market users are likely taking a peptide tested rigorously in sarcoidosis but not in the diabetic and aging populations who would drive demand.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A Phase 3 RCT in diabetic peripheral neuropathy (the most common indication sought) with ≥200 participants, pre-registered, blinded, and measuring pain relief (NEUROPAD, pain scales) as primary outcome—not corneal nerve fiber size—would clarify whether effect is real and clinically meaningful. Similarly, a formal meta-analysis of existing RCTs with published protocols and heterogeneity assessment would determine whether the three neuropathy trials point in the same direction or contradict each other.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Péptido inyectable derivado de eritropoyetina; apunta a vías de reparación inmunológica y nerviosa.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Cibinetida (también conocida como ARA290) es un péptido corto—una cadena de aminoácidos, los componentes básicos de las proteínas. Fue diseñada a partir de eritropoyetina, una hormona natural que tu cuerpo produce para impulsar la producción de glóbulos rojos, pero cibinetida elimina esa función de impulso sanguíneo y conserva solo las partes de reparación nerviosa y calma inmunológica. Se presenta como una preparación inyectable para investigación y uso en ensayos clínicos.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Se une al receptor de reparación innata, señalizando calma inmunológica y protección nerviosa.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Cibinetida se une a un receptor llamado receptor de reparación innata (IRR)—imagina un receptor como una cerradura en la superficie de una célula en la que encaja una llave específica. Cuando cibinetida se acopla a esa cerradura, envía una señal dentro de la célula que amortigua la inflamación (la respuesta de alarma del sistema inmunológico) y activa vías protectoras y de reparación en células nerviosas y células inmunológicas. En estudios en animales, se ha demostrado que reduce las señales de dolor afectando los canales TRPV1 (puertas moleculares que detectan calor y dolor) y protege las células pancreáticas del estrés y el rechazo. El mecanismo parece funcionar calmando el sistema inmunológico innato—la rama de rápida actuación y no específica que puede dañar los tejidos si está hiperactivada—en lugar de impulsar los conteos de células sanguíneas como hace la eritropoyetina original.
explanation_es.safety_line: Efectos secundarios leves reportados en ensayos cortos; los datos a largo plazo e interacciones farmacológicas siguen siendo limitados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos humanos recuperados fueron a corto plazo (típicamente semanas a pocos meses) e informaron tolerabilidad leve y transitoria en los participantes estudiados. Se observaron reacciones en el sitio de inyección y síntomas menores consistentes con modulación inmunológica, pero no surgieron señales de seguridad graves en estos conjuntos de datos limitados. Sin embargo, los ensayos fueron estrechos en alcance—incluyeron principalmente a adultos con condiciones específicas (sarcoidosis, diabetes) y no se extendieron a duraciones más largas o poblaciones diversas.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo (meses a años de uso) no ha sido estudiada adecuadamente en humanos; todos los ensayos recuperados fueron a corto plazo.
Las interacciones farmacológicas con inmunosupresores u otros agentes moduladores inmunológicos no están documentadas en los registros proporcionados; desconocidas.
El uso en embarazo, adolescentes menores de 18 años y pacientes con enfermedad renal o hepática grave no ha sido probado y no se reporta en ningún ensayo recuperado.

Como terapéutico de péptidos, se administra típicamente por inyección; las reacciones alérgicas o en el sitio de inyección son teóricamente posibles pero no fueron comparadas sistemáticamente con placebo en los estudios proporcionados.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Cibinetida es un péptido bastante grande y que ama el agua (PM 1257, XLogP −7.7). Su lipofilia negativa significa que se disuelve fácilmente en agua pero no cruza la barrera hematoencefálica o la piel fácilmente por sí sola, por lo que debe inyectarse en lugar de tomarse por vía oral. El peso molecular alto también significa que no sobrevivirá al ácido estomacal, y su estructura limita qué tan lejos en el cuerpo puede difundir pasivamente—depende del transporte activo y la inyección para llegar a sus células objetivo.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro ensayos clínicos aleatorizados controlados (EAC) humanos y dos estudios en animales examinaron cibinetida para dolor nervioso y daño de fibras nerviosas pequeñas. Un EAC de 2017 (n=64) en pacientes con pérdida de fibras nerviosas pequeñas asociada a sarcoidosis encontró que cibinetida mejoró la abundancia de fibras nerviosas corneales (un marcador medible de salud nerviosa en el ojo). Un EAC de 2015 reportó mejoría en síntomas neuropáticos y marcadores metabólicos en poblaciones similares. Estudios en animales (2016, 2014) mostraron que el compuesto alivió las señales de dolor al dirigirse a los canales TRPV1 y reducir la inflamación en modelos experimentales de lesión nerviosa.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cuatro ensayos humanos proporcionan confianza moderada, pero el tamaño de muestra verificado más grande fue de 64 participantes en un estudio, y ningún metanálisis armonizó los resultados. La evidencia es genuina pero modesta en escala y duración.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios humanos y seis estudios en animales investigaron el efecto de cibinetida en la inflamación. El EAC de 2013 en pacientes con sarcoidosis y un estudio observacional de 2018 en poblaciones similares ambos notaron reducciones en marcadores inflamatorios relacionados con daño nervioso. El trabajo en animales (2021, 2020, 2017, 2016) demostró que cibinetida amortiguó la activación de células inmunológicas innatas, redujo señales proinflamatorias y protegió el tejido (islotes, intestino) del daño inmunológico en modelos de colitis y trasplante.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Los datos humanos son limitados (dos estudios, tamaños de muestra mayormente no reportados), pero el trabajo mecanístico en animales es consistente y respalda una vía antiinflamatoria. La precisión no está confirmada porque la mayoría de los resúmenes no reportaron números exactos de participantes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos humanos y cuatro estudios en animales abordaron el azúcar en sangre y el control de glucosa. Un EAC de Fase 2 de 2020 examinó cibinetida para edema macular diabético (daño ocular por diabetes). Un EAC de 2017 (n=64) en pacientes con sarcoidosis reportó mejoras metabólicas junto con ganancias en fibras nerviosas. Estudios en animales (2021, 2020, 2017) encontraron que cibinetida protegió las células de islotes pancreáticos (que producen insulina) del estrés, mejoró la función del trasplante de islotes y redujo el daño inflamatorio a los tejidos productores de glucosa.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Tres ensayos humanos y datos consistentes en animales sugieren un efecto real, pero la muestra humana verificada fue de 64 participantes en un estudio; la mayoría de los resúmenes omitieron números exactos, por lo que el tamaño total de muestra humana es incierto. Ningún análisis agrupado confirmó consistencia entre ensayos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios humanos y tres estudios en animales se enfocaron en resultados de ojo y visión. Un EAC de Fase 2 de 2020 probó cibinetida para edema macular diabético (líquido y pérdida de visión por diabetes). Un EAC de 2017 (n=64) en pacientes con sarcoidosis mostró mejoría en la abundancia de fibras nerviosas corneales, un biomarcador de salud de nervios corneales. Un EAC de 2013 reportó mejoras corneales similares en neuropatía de fibras pequeñas asociada a sarcoidosis. Un estudio de 2018 validó la evaluación de fibras nerviosas corneales como marcador clínico de respuesta al tratamiento. Los estudios en animales protegieron injertos de islotes y tejido pancreático, apoyando mecanismos que pueden beneficiar indirectamente las complicaciones metabólicas del ojo.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cuatro ensayos humanos proporcionan apoyo moderado, pero la cohorte verificada más grande fue de 64 participantes en un estudio. La mayoría de los resúmenes no reportaron tamaños de muestra finales, y ningún metanálisis confirmó consistencia de resultados de visión u ojo específico entre ensayos.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia para cibinetida se ancla en cuatro ensayos clínicos aleatorizados controlados (EAC) humanos, todos conducidos entre 2013 y 2020, junto con estudios mecanísticos en animales (modelos de dolor e inflamación en roedores, modelos de trasplante y pancreáticos). Los ensayos humanos fueron generalmente a corto plazo (semanas a pocos meses) e involucraron adultos con condiciones autoinmunes o metabólicas específicas (sarcoidosis, diabetes). La mayoría de los resúmenes no reportan números completos de participantes, por lo que la muestra humana verificada total es modesta (al menos ~64 en un ensayo). El trabajo en animales es robusto y consistente pero no puede traducirse directamente a humanos sin pruebas adicionales.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen ensayos en adolescentes, niños o individuos embarazadas, ni en pacientes con enfermedad renal o hepática avanzada—por lo que si cibinetida es segura o efectiva en estos grupos sigue siendo desconocido. Ningún estudio más largo que unos pocos meses parece estar en el conjunto de datos, por lo que la durabilidad del beneficio y la seguridad acumulativa durante años no han sido probadas. Los ensayos humanos se agrupan en torno a sarcoidosis y diabetes; la eficacia en otras condiciones neuropáticas o inflamatorias no está documentada en los registros proporcionados. La optimización de dosis y los efectos inmunológicos a largo plazo (por ejemplo, si la dosificación repetida altera el estado basal del sistema inmunológico) no se abordan en los resúmenes recuperados.

appraisal_es.headline: La totalidad de la base de evidencia humana para cibinetida consiste en ~3 RCT con solo uno reportando tamaño de muestra (n=64); no existen análisis agrupados, la mayoría de afirmaciones descansan en modelos animales, y la significancia clínica de las medidas de fibras nerviosas corneales permanece sin validar.

concerns.issue: Subnotificación severa de tamaños de muestra humanos
concerns.detail: En los cuatro desenlaces (neuropatía, inflamación, glucosa en sangre, ojo/visión), solo 1 de 15 estudios humanos reporta un tamaño de muestra extraíble (n=64 en el RCT de 2017). El motor nota que 'la mayoría de resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra', lo que significa que el denominador verdadero para la evidencia humana es desconocido. Esto impide calcular la precisión verdadera, detectar sesgo de publicación, y evaluar si estudios insuficientemente potenciados están impulsando las calificaciones 'moderadas'.

concerns.issue: Dependencia pesada de modelos animales con validez traslacional poco clara
concerns.detail: Para inflamación (6 de 8 estudios), glucosa en sangre (4 de 7 estudios), y ojo/visión (3 de 7 estudios), los estudios en animales dominan la base de evidencia. Ninguno de los estudios animales reporta si fueron registrados a priori, cegados, o prepotenciados. El salto de 'ARA 290 reduce la activación de macrófagos en ratones' (animal de 2016) a 'cibinetida controla la glucosa en sangre en humanos' no está conectado por datos mecanísticos—solo suposición.

concerns.issue: Desenlaces subrogados (nervios corneales) reemplazan puntos finales clínicos
concerns.detail: Tres de los cuatro RCT humanos (2017, 2018, 2020) listan abundancia de fibras nerviosas corneales o tamaño de fibras nerviosas corneales como su medida primaria o reportada. Estos son biomarcadores morfológicos, no alivio de dolor clínico, mejora de visión, o control glucémico. Ningún estudio valida que la mejora de fibras nerviosas corneales predice beneficio real relevante para el paciente.

concerns.issue: Sin efectos agrupados extraíbles y sin consenso metaanalítico
concerns.detail: El motor nota 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble' en los cuatro desenlaces y señala 'Inconsistencia: existen varios estudios pero ningún análisis agrupado confirma que concuerden' para glucosa en sangre y ojo/visión. Esto significa que los estudios no han sido sintetizados formalmente, por lo que los lectores no pueden saber si los tres RCT sobre neuropatía concuerdan entre sí o si la heterogeneidad está impulsando los resultados.

concerns.issue: Especificidad de la población limita la generalizabilidad
concerns.detail: Las dos cohortes de RCT humanos más grandes (2013, 2017) reclutaron pacientes con pérdida de fibras nerviosas pequeñas asociada a sarcoidosis—una enfermedad rara. El ensayo de DME de 2020 es separado. No existe evidencia de cibinetida en neuropatía diabética común, neuropatía de fibras pequeñas idiopática, u otras neuropatías prevalentes. La eficacia en sarcoidosis no predice eficacia en las poblaciones con más probabilidad de buscar acceso en el mercado gris.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: La literatura animal propone que cibinetida activa el receptor de reparación innata (IRR) para suprimir la activación de macrófagos y reducir citocinas inflamatorias, lo que podría plausiblemente reducir el dolor neuropático y apoyar la función de islotes. Sin embargo, este mecanismo se prueba solo en modelos animales (colitis, neuritis autoinmune, ensayos de macrófagos); ningún estudio humano mide la señalización de IRR, niveles de citocinas, o vincula la activación de la vía con los desenlaces clínicos reportados. El salto de 'ARA 290 inhibe la activación de macrófagos in vitro' a 'cibinetida mejora el edema macular diabético' implica múltiples suposiciones no expresadas sobre penetración tisular, biología de vías humanas, y si el mecanismo opera en los estados de enfermedad estudiados.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico notaría que los cuatro desenlaces están calificados como 'moderados'—el nivel más bajo por encima de 'bajo'—y que cada calificación descansa en una base endeble: 1–3 RCT humanos de tamaño de muestra total desconocido, usando biomarcadores subrogados (nervios corneales) en lugar de desenlaces clínicos, en poblaciones de enfermedad rara (sarcoidosis). Ningún metanálisis confirma que estos ensayos concuerden. El aparente amplitud de beneficio (neuropatía, inflamación, glucosa en sangre, visión) en diversos tejidos se asemeja a un 'mecanismo en búsqueda de una enfermedad' en lugar de evidencia convergente—y está explicada completamente por modelos animales que frecuentemente no translan. Los usuarios del mercado gris probablemente están tomando un péptido probado rigurosamente en sarcoidosis pero no en poblaciones diabéticas y envejecidas que impulsarían la demanda.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo de Fase 3 en neuropatía periférica diabética (la indicación más común buscada) con ≥200 participantes, preregistrado, cegado, y midiendo alivio del dolor (NEUROPAD, escalas de dolor) como desenlace primario—no tamaño de fibras nerviosas corneales—aclararía si el efecto es real y clínicamente significativo. Similarmente, un metanálisis formal de RCT existentes con protocolos publicados y evaluación de heterogeneidad determinaría si los tres ensayos de neuropatía apuntan en la misma dirección o se contradicen.
